target_customer: Airlines that would buy or order supersonic airliners, plus government and defense customers
problem: Long-haul air travel has been no faster since Concorde retired. Boom set out to bring back supersonic passenger flight at lower fares.
business_model: Aircraft manufacturer: pre-orders and deposits from airlines, venture and later large private funding; Superpower turbines add an energy product

founders.name: Blake Scholl
founders.background_notes: YC page and Boom's site give no personal background. Boom's timeline says he founded the company in his Denver basement in 2014.

competitors.name: Aerion
competitors.what: Reno-based developer of a supersonic business jet
competitors.traction_then: Named as pursuing supersonic flight in a December 2016 article; no orders or revenue stated

competitors.name: Spike Aerospace
competitors.what: Boston-based developer of a supersonic jet
competitors.traction_then: Named as pursuing supersonic passenger flight in a December 2016 article

competitors.name: Gulfstream
competitors.what: Business jet maker quietly studying supersonic business jet concepts
competitors.traction_then: Concept studies only per the article

technical_complexity.rationale: Designing, certifying and building a Mach 2 class airliner and engine needs deep aerospace engineering and regulatory approval. The company's first demonstrator XB-1 only flew in March 2024 and broke the sound barrier in January 2025.

defensibility.rationale: Capital needs, certification and engineering talent make entry very hard; competitors such as Aerion later collapsed per search results, but the dated source for that was not opened.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The December 2016 article said Boeing and Dassault had dabbled and Gulfstream was studying concepts; none shipped a competing supersonic airliner. Boom partnered with suppliers and customers instead.

market_need_then: A December 2016 Fortune article reported orders for 25 aircraft including 10 from Virgin, and a projected demand of 1,300 supersonic jetliners over ten years from 2023. Those are company projections, not independent demand data.

identity.logo: Wordmark and mark available in the press kit; design details not described in sources
identity.visual_style: Aviation livery focused, with partner liveries shown on Overture renders
identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline It's About Time on the site

branding.brand_signature: Baby Boom nickname for XB-1 and the public Overture livery design contest
branding.community_and_virality: Boom ran a public contest inviting fans to design Overture liveries, per its own site. An agency, Manual, says it advanced Boom's brand identity.

brand_strength.rationale: Short evocative name suits the product and the company runs fan engagement such as the livery contest, but sources do not show brand as a driver of growth over technical milestones.

outcome_analysis: Boom raised a 33 million dollar Series A in March 2017 that brought total funding to about 41 million, then kept raising while building the XB-1 demonstrator. The demonstrator first flew in March 2024 and broke the sound barrier in January 2025, which was a major technical proof point. The company later reports an order book of 130 aircraft and a new Superpower turbine line. The sources do not give later round sizes or valuations, so funding coverage is partial.
notes: Seed amount is unverified: aggregators range from 2.1 to 6 million in March 2016, so no amount is recorded; the seed investors are those TechCrunch calls earlier investors. The 41 million total implies about 8 million before the Series A. Competitor source is dated December 2016, about nine months after the Winter 2016 batch start. Later rounds (2020s) were not researched in sources opened. Founding year 2014 is from Boom's own timeline as summarized in search.
